title: Triage workflow + SLO flex steering for enterprise dedicated capacity intake
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Problem: Enterprise sales and solutions teams are bringing varied dedicated capacity requests with inconsistent SLA expectations (latency SLOs, reserved throughput, GPU class preferences and burst policies). Current intake is ad-hoc and causes repeated rework between Sales/SE, Product, and Eng. Goal: Define a deterministic triage workflow (questionnaire + decision tree + steering rules) that maps customer-request signals to an initial SLO/throughput/GPU recommendation, plus a standard escalation path for edge cases. Scope: intake form, scoring rubric, automated recommendation engine spec (heuristic prototype), handoff checklist for Dedicated onboarding, and playbook for SRE/Eng when requests require deviating from default guardrails. Out of scope: pricing negotiation, legal contract templates, or building final automation — this ticket produces the playbook + spec + acceptance tests to enable engineering to implement automation in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: A clear intake questionnaire covering workload shape, peak TPS, latency target, cold/hot KV patterns, data residency, and failure tolerance is published and reviewed by Sales, SE, and Eng.
A scoring rubric maps intake fields to a recommended GPU class, reserved throughput band, and an initial SLO band (latency P95 target and availability tier).
Decision tree for escalation cases (multi-region, regulatory, burst > 10x baseline, sustained 24/7 high throughput) documented with owners and SLAs for manual review.
Playbook includes a standard ‘handoff packet’ format (intake + recommended config + risk notes + required infra changes) and a one-page executive summary template for customer conversations.
Pilot: run rubric against 7 recent enterprise intake examples and produce a runbook entry showing alignment (3/7 automated recommendations accepted by Eng/SE without changes).
Stakeholder sign-off: Sales Lead, Solutions Engineering Lead, Head of Infrastructure, and two enterprise customers sign off on pilot findings.
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Agreed to use a three-band reserved throughput taxonomy (baseline, burstable, dedicated-high) instead of continuous numeric buckets to reduce negotiation friction. -- Decision by PM, SE, Eng
2026-03-02: Chose to prioritize latency P95 as primary SLO signal for initial mapping; availability tiers remain binary (standard/SLA-backed). -- Decision by PM + SRE
2026-03-08: For GPU class recommendation use workload fingerprint + model sequence length heuristic; fall back to customer-preferred GPU when compliance is explicit. -- Decision by Eng Lead
follow_up_tasks: Create ENG ticket to implement recommendation engine prototype (heuristic rules) - target rollout in dedicated-2026.05
Design to produce the handoff packet template (Figma) and upload to Drive
Ops to add a new 'triage' label and create onboarding checklist in the Console for accepted configs
Legal to review the executive summary template for compliance disclaimers
